scalars.scalar_value: Two (2+) or more years of CNA experience in an acute care setting.

items.item_text: BART or BLS at time of hire with commitment to get BART within six (6) months of hire date.
Must be able to work various hours and locations based on business needs.
Employment is subject to a criminal background check and pre-employment physical.

Per diem shift requirement is an average of 1 shift per week per 4-week schedule. Must be available 1 weekend shift per 4-week schedule and required to work one of the following holidays per year (Memorial Day, July 4th or Labor Day) per a rotational schedule or department needs. Additionally, must work one of the following holidays per year (Thanksgiving, Christmas or New Year’s Eve) per rotational schedule or department needs.
Two (2+) or more years of CNA experience in an acute care setting.
Experience with EPIC, UCSD Paging & Scheduling Systems.

Under the supervision of the Registered Nurse, the CNA supports the continuum of care by providing basic patient care and assistance with activities of daily living. Performs uncomplicated technical procedures. Utilizes a variety of technical equipment and supplies. Provides basic patient care support: patient transport, specimen and blood and blood products transport, and inventory management.

This position requires initiative, the ability to prioritize demands and the ability to work in a team environment. Participates in collaborative team environment, including: training and evaluation of peers; scheduling of work; and assisting the administrative functions of the unit.

Jacobs Medical Center Hematology and Cellular Therapy unit offers the only Blood and Marrow Transplant program in San Diego that is affiliated with a renowned School of Medicine and accredited by the Foundation for the Accreditation of Hematopoietic Therapy (FACT). We focus on Blood and Marrow Transplant, cellular therapies such as CAR-T, and serving patients with hematological malignancies on our 36-bed private room unit. The growing list of diseases, as well as non-malignant conditions we treat includes: lymphoma and Hodgkin’s disease, acute and chronic leukemia, multiple myeloma, myelodysplastic syndrome, testicular cancer, aplastic anemia, auto-immune and genetic diseases.
Demonstrate ability to prioritize tasks effectively, identify and communicate patient status and/or safety changes such as vital signs abnormalities in a timely, clear, and efficient manner.
